slug_convention: The :latest tag is the default for any model and MUST be omitted from model names and slugs. Only explicit non-default tags (e.g. :14b, :q8_0, :bf16) are included.

methodology_notes.layer2_raw_vs_chat: Layer 2 (HumanEval-CS, 158 tasks) historically uses scripts/benchmark_coding_layer2.py which calls /api/generate with raw:true. This bypasses the model's chat template / RENDERER / PARSER and sends the C# function signature as a raw completion prefix. Completion-friendly models (granite4, OmniCoder, qwen-coder, gemma3, shenwen-coderV2) handle this well and score 25-50%. Chat-tuned and thinking-default models (gemma4 family, gpt-oss, glm-4.7-flash-reap, lfm2.5-thinking, LFM2, phi4-mini) score 1-10% because they cannot interpret the raw prefix without their chat wrappers. For these models, also run scripts/benchmark_coding_layer2_chat.py which uses /api/chat (template applied, num_predict=4096, num_ctx=8192, reasoning_effort=low for gpt-oss). Chat-mode results are stored in coding-{slug}-chat.json and listed alongside the raw-mode score in this file. Headline 'L2' for chat-tuned models should use the chat-mode score; raw-mode is a methodological footnote.
methodology_notes.layer3_think_variants: Layer 3 (.NET, 50 tasks) coding runner defaults to think:false via task_runner.py. To run a paired think:true variant, set CODING_BENCH_THINK=true; the runner suffixes the checkpoint with '-think' so both variants are preserved (coding-{slug}.json and coding-{slug}-think.json). Some models (granite4 family, qwen3-coder-next) reject think:true with 'does not support thinking' and produce a 0/50 file that should be deleted. Other models (gpt-oss, lfm2.5-thinking, glm-4.7-flash-reap-toolfix) ignore think:false and still emit reasoning; their no-think baselines are effectively think runs and the -think variant is redundant. See memory/project_ollama_think_quirks.md for the full matrix.

backend_notes.qwen3.5:9b: T5500 champion tier: 38.87 tok/s, 5/5 quality (old 5-pt metric), 8.2GB VRAM, PPL 3.89 on Ollama 0.18.1. CODING (figures 2026-06-24, qwen3.5:9b Q4_K_M 6.6GB, gen on T5500 RTX 3060 via OLLAMA_HOST, build/test on Framework — same cross-machine setup as Qwythos so directly comparable): L2 CHAT 67/158 (0.424) — trusted L2 number; L2 RAW 42/158 (0.266) — ARTIFACT (raw completion mode on this instruct-tuned model emits Java-ish code when unanchored, e.g. `public static void main`/`Scanner`; use L2-CHAT instead). Fresh same-day re-run after hardening the raw harness; the prior 61/158 was a 2026-04-17 figure from an EARLIER model pull (current build re-pulled 2026-06-23, digest 6488c96fa5fa), so the two are NOT comparable. L3 (.NET): no-think 3/50 (0.0545 weighted), think 1/50 (0.0182) — THINK HURT L3 (median gen 8s->107s, no quality gain), USE THE NO-THINK BASELINE. Failures are genuine: 46/50 build-fail with real code generated, 0 harness/timeout errors, healthy gen times; the passing tasks are all Blazor. Think behaviour: CLEAN — thinks by default, thinking emitted to a SEPARATE 'thinking' API field (NOT <think> in content), think:false suppresses it and works; content always clean so coding extractors need no special handling. KEY COMPARISON (base vs empero-ai Qwythos-9B fine-tune, BOTH same cross-machine setup → apples-to-apples): base wins L2-chat (67 vs 62) but the fine-tune marginally wins L2-raw (42 vs 50), L3 no-think (3 vs 6) and L3 think (1 vs 4). All gaps are small (<=4 tasks/50 on L3) on two weak coders — the 'Mythos' fine-tune neither clearly helped nor clearly hurt single-shot C# coding; both are poor at idiomatic .NET (<=6/50 L3). This is exactly why the differentiator for this model class is the agentic/tool/long-context Layer 4 suite (docs/agentic-tool-longcontext-benchmark-plan.md), not single-shot code gen.

backend_notes.gemma4:12b: Framework RTX 3060 eGPU, Ollama 0.30.5 (gemma4:12b needs >=0.30.5; 0.24.0 returns 412, and 0.30.5 release notes fix a gemma4:12b FP-exception crash). 12B DENSE multimodal, released 2026-06-03, 256K native context, default tag = 12b-it-q4_K_M (7.63GB). PASSES Framework gate: at num_ctx=131072 loads 100% GPU (7.63GB VRAM) at ~18.6 tok/s (warm; 13.6 tok/s when GPU thermally loaded — thermal-dependent, both >10). CRITICAL: the model's DEFAULT 256K context overflows 12GB → partial offload → 5.58 tok/s (FAILS gate); ALWAYS pin num_ctx<=131072 on this 12GB GPU (throughput script now has -NumCtx). Quick quality 11/11. Coding L2 chat-mode (HumanEval-CS, think:false): 95/158 (0.601) — STRONG broad coder, beats mistral-small (0.38)/GLM-4.5-Air-REAP (0.52)/qwen3.6 (0.49). Coding L3 (.NET): think:false 5/50 (0.091), think:true@4096 6/50 (0.109) — BOTH weak. think:true is budget-starved (model emits ~2000+ thinking tokens; 10/50 tasks 'Empty code after extraction' at the harness 4096 cap). A think:true@8192 ceiling re-run of the 10 starved tasks scored 0/10 (8 still empty) — so the weak complex-.NET result is a GENUINE capability/runaway-reasoning limit, NOT mere budget starvation. Verdict: excellent gate-passing 128K generalist + strong simple-coding/tool model, but a POOR fit for reasoning-heavy .NET on a 13-tps box (verbose reasoning = poor effective time-to-code). For .NET coding on Framework prefer faster perfect-quality models (glm-4.7-flash, qwen3-coder-next). Compared against the Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL dynamic quant (see gemma4-12b-ud-q4kxl): DEAD TIE on quality (both 11/11 quick, both 95/158 L2) and effectively tied on speed (q4_K_M 18.6 vs UD 19.6 tok/s, ~6% within run-to-run/thermal variance) → KEEP the official q4_K_M (no custom-Modelfile/HF-GGUF dependency, official updates). Higher quants (q5/q6/q8/mxfp8/nvfp4/bf16) offload on 12GB → Strix Halo candidates, not Framework. Headline coding number for cross-machine comparison should use think:true L3 once a larger-budget standard is set; quote L2-chat 0.601 as the broad-coding figure.

backend_notes.vibethinker-csharp-p1-5k: FINE-TUNE (phase-1 proof-of-life, 2026-06-22). VibeThinker-3B + LoRA (r=32/a=64, 7 target modules, bf16, packing seq2048, adamw_torch, 3 epochs) on 5k completion-style C# examples from The Stack v1 dedup (scripts/lora/build_stack_csharp_dataset.py; 4500 train / 500 holdout). Trained on T5500 (RTX 3060, C:\Python311 cu126 env, ~3h20m, 150 steps): loss 2.77->1.13, token-acc 0.656->0.85, clean convergence. Deployed via GGUF (f16, convert_hf_to_gguf on T5500) -> ollama create (GGUF import; Ollama's safetensors converter fails 'untrusted mount point' on T5500 — see PLATFORM_QUIRKS). RESULTS (gen on T5500 GPU via OLLAMA_HOST, build/test on Framework): Coding L2 CHAT 20/158 (0.127); Coding L3 (.NET) 0/50. VERDICT: did NOT clear the >=40/158 phase-1 gate, and is a SLIGHT REGRESSION vs base VibeThinker (25/158) — narrow 5k completion-style LoRA mildly eroded base reasoning (catastrophic forgetting) while teaching the desired raw-C#-output behavior (no <think>, no prose/markdown — confirmed). L2 failure mix: 85 build-fail (model syntax errors + inconsistent output format, e.g. sometimes emits its own Main), 50 build-OK-wrong-answer, 2 runtime exc, 1 timeout, 20 PASS. L3 0/50 expected: phase-1 did not target ASP.NET/EF/MassTransit APIs (phase-2 goal). NOTE: required an L2-chat harness fix (commit 408b62f) to handle bare re-emitted methods (no class Problem wrapper) — without it the fine-tune scored an artifactual 0/158. NEXT ITER: scale phase-1 data (50k+), mitigate forgetting (lower lr/rank or mix instruction+diverse data), improve Stack example quality (many train bodies were low-quality raw functions). Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-21-vibethinker-csharp-phase1.md.

Deployed Q4_K_M (matches BASE quant for apples-to-apples; iter-1 was f16): merge -> convert_hf_to_gguf -> ollama create FROM gguf on T5500. RESULTS (gen on T5500 GPU via OLLAMA_HOST, build/test on Framework): Coding L2 CHAT 22/158 (0.139); Coding L3 (.NET) 0/50. 3-WAY: base VibeThinker 25/158 (0.158) > iter2 22/158 > iter1 (vibethinker-csharp-p1-5k) 20/158 (0.127). VERDICT: iter2 beats iter1 (+2) but STILL BELOW base (-3); >=40/158 gate MISSED. L2 mix: 22 PASS, 91 build-fail (58% — still the dominant failure; cleaner 50k data did NOT materially fix C# syntax vs iter1's 85), 41 build-OK-wrong-answer (assertion), 4 runtime exc/OOM. L3 0/50 expected: phase-1 (broad Stack C#) does not target ASP.NET/EF/MassTransit/Blazor APIs — that is the phase-2 goal. Behavior learned (both iters): emits raw C# (no <think>/prose/markdown). DEPLOY LESSONS (see PLATFORM_QUIRKS): (1) detached remote training over ssh must redirect output to a remote FILE and launch via Task Scheduler (held-ssh + `-u` -> broken-pipe-on-flush death; schtasks escapes the ssh job object); (2) `ollama create` 'failed to validate GGUF with llama-quantize' was DISK (validation needs scratch; freeing orphan blobs fixed it), not a bad GGUF. BENCHMARK CAVEAT: this run was on a degraded Framework host (C: ~full + a game over RustDesk); cold dotnet builds hit 16-73s so the 30s default timeout mis-scored valid runs as timeouts — re-run with L2_RUN_TIMEOUT_S/L3_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S/L3_TEST_TIMEOUT_S=150 gave the valid numbers above. NEXT: phase-2 (think+code, L3-targeted ASP.NET/EF/MassTransit data) per plan, OR address the build-fail rate (output-format consistency, harder syntax filtering) before scaling further.
